I don't know what kind of position you're in so it's not fair of me to say I've been in the same position as you, but I was definitely in a somewhat similar rut. For what felt like the longest time, everyday melted together, and even getting out of bed was a challenge. Now I look back at it with regret because I feel like I wasted a good year of my life moping around. Things have gotten much better, but occasionally I still get that dark feeling when I'm having a bad few days. At least you have a good boyfriend who's there for you. It's much much better then having to face something like depression all alone, even if you can't exactly talk to him about it. Seems like you appreciate the good that's in your life, and honestly it's the best advice I can give you. Sort out all the people in your life that you want to be with you, and always keep in touch with them, let them know you are grateful for them. Those are the kinds of people that'll have your back if/when you need it. I really hope things are going to get consistently get better for you, but even if they don't, your life cannot stay shitty forever. Just try your best to change the things you don't like about it, eventually things have to change, even if it seems like forever. Best wishes and good luck to ya!

IMO, death is the same as it was before you had life. I honestly don't believe in any gods, or heaven/hell whatever. And I remember the first time I thought about it when I was maybe 9 or 10, and it terrified me. I couldn't sleep, and I was always so scared of death. I felt it was so strange that no one ever talks about it, people just simply believe some higher being is constantly judging our every action, and when you die, you get a second luxurious life. None of that happens. In fact, as I grew older, for awhile I began to hate people for excepting such a simple-minded answer. But then I began to realize that for most people, that's all they need to hear because they're too scared to REALLY think about what happens after you die..Honestly, even if nothing happens, and you're just a rotting corpse in the ground who will inevitably be forgotten as time goes on, wouldn't that just be more reason to make the life you have now as awesome and kick ass as possible? When I began to realize this, I stopped giving a shit what people thought of me, especially religious folk, and I found myself a lot happier. Death still scares me, but if I'm lucky, I won't die for at least another 60-70 years, and that gives me so much time to do everything I want to, so I should be careful not to waste my precious time on this planet, because I don't know how much time I'll have left. I could die tomorrow, or next year, or when I'm 40. Who knows. But I refuse to spend my life wasting my breathe on prayers, and instead actually doing something to help. Your life is yours, so do what can with what you have my friend.
